summary: Douglas County, Missouri tower: five acres bought in 1962 and a 100-foot steel tower erected that year; a 2015 MDC plan lists it in use for fire detection.

facts.status_note: The 2015 MDC plan lists the tower in use for fire detection. No source gives its current status.

events.note: Conservation Commission acquired five acres for the Squires Tower site on February 3, 1962, for $150
2015 MDC management plan: tower used by the Forestry Division for fire detection

corrections.why: The Conservation Commission bought the land in 1962. The 2015 plan, issued by the Missouri Department of Conservation, names MDC as the manager.

sources.title: Douglas & Wright County Towersites Area Management Plan, 2015

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The 1962 facts come from a compiled list quoting annual reports. The 2015 plan is the latest source found, so the tower's status is known only as of 2015. A Facebook post by the Missouri Conservation History and Equipment page says the tower is still listed as climbable. The page could not be fetched, so it is not used. Do not add an access or climbing claim until MDC confirms it. Access is left unset.
